gap: No result ChatGPT got states that no named reviewer has published a measured 4K 144 Hz run through any standalone KVM with a MacBook. The only named review of a KVM that ChatGPT showed (SolderMag on the TESmart DKS202-M24) says it did no hands-on switching or latency tests. The only named Mac-plus-KVM report found ran at 1440p 120 Hz, not 4K 144 Hz. The monitor-KVM route does have independent measurements: Profesional Review measured the Gigabyte M27UP at 11 ms click-to-pixel with Nvidia LDAT and 427 cd/m².
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited: the TESmart HDMI 2.1 gaming KVM guide, TESmart's DSC blog post, the DKS202-M24, DKS202-MC24 and HKS202-M24 product pages, the TESmart HDMI-vs-DP blog post, the L1Techs KVM FAQ and the Level1Techs single-monitor 2-computer store page. Every 4K 144 Hz figure on them is the maker's own spec. The TESmart guide cites no third-party lab and says the result 'still depends on the selected monitor inputs and the complete chain'. The L1 FAQ's only measured data are cable eye-pattern tests and hotkey scan times. The L1 store page lists 4K120, plus 144 Hz only at 1440p. None of them says that independent Mac testing at 4K 144 Hz is missing, and none gives a measured figure for the monitor-KVM alternative.
decides: This supports our page's current pick of the monitor's built-in KVM over a standalone switch. Every standalone KVM ChatGPT showed (UGREEN, Level1Techs, TESmart HKS201/DKS202/HKS202/HDK202, StarTech D86A2) rests only on its maker's spec, and the one Mac owner who reported a result through a KVM got 1440p 120 Hz. The Gigabyte M27UP has named measurements (11 ms LDAT, 427 cd/m², 1131:1 contrast). Its 18 W USB-C power is a limit, so the Mac keeps its own charger. The finding doesn't name a standalone KVM that works. It shows that none has been proven, and that is the case for the monitor route.

findings.label: Click-to-pixel latency (Profesional Review, José Antonio Castillo)
findings.note: Measured with Nvidia LDAT in Doom Eternal at 1920×1080, 320 Hz, over HDMI 2.1, on an i9-12900K and RTX 4080 bench. Review published 2025-11-05. This is the monitor alone, not a KVM chain.

findings.label: Brightness and contrast, UHD mode (Profesional Review)
findings.note: Measured at the panel centre. The review says edge cells stay above 350 but below 400 nits.

findings.label: USB-C power delivery (as listed in the Profesional Review review)
findings.note: Comes from the review's port list ('USB Type-C (DisplayPort 1.4, Power Delivery 18W)'), not a wattmeter reading. The conclusion says 18 W cannot power Max-Q laptops. The review describes the KVM (USB-B plus USB-C for two computers) but reports no KVM or Mac test.

findings.label: Independent hands-on testing (SolderMag)
findings.value: None performed: no switching, latency, display-retention or adaptive-sync measurements
findings.source_title: TESmart DKS202-M24 Review: High-Refresh KVM, Heavy Wiring – SolderMag
findings.note: Page updated 2026-08-17. Quote: 'We have not independently verified dual 4K144 operation.' It also says the KVM 'cannot bypass the Mac's external-display limit'.

findings.label: Mac refresh actually run through the KVM (MacRumors forum user timmah339)
findings.value: 1440p (scaled) at 120 Hz on two 4K Thunderbolt displays; 144 Hz not tested
findings.note: An owner's report dated 2025-03-25 with an M4 Mac mini and an M3 MacBook Pro, not a lab measurement. The poster wrote 'I think it should work for a single display at 144Hz' but did not confirm it. The KVM charges only the active computer.

findings.label: Maker's rated refresh (the page ChatGPT cited)

findings.source_title: 1.4 Display Port KVM Switch - Single Monitor - Two Computer — Level1Techs Store
